text: We evaluated mixup between weak-labeled examples (mixup_alpha = 0.4) on the cosmos_qa testbed, measuring performance gap recovered (PGR). Across num_seeds = 3 seeds, the method attained a PGR of 0.9 with a standard error of 0.14. Taken at face value, this indicates that the student recovers a large share of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling on this task, but the estimate carries substantial uncertainty: with only three seeds, the standard error of 0.14 is wide relative to the quantity being measured, and the sampling distribution of such a small set of runs is poorly characterized. No baseline PGR was supplied in this experiment, so we cannot characterize the result as an improvement over any alternative weak-to-strong training procedure, nor can we attribute the observed value specifically to the mixup intervention rather than to other aspects of the setup. The finding should be treated as preliminary and worth replicating with more seeds and an explicit baseline arm before any comparative claim is made.
